subject: Orchestrator reconciliation lag during private VPC rolling upgrade — customer action items
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:52:00-08:00
Subject: [Incident] Orchestrator reconciliation backlog detected on MediSync private VPC

Hannah / Marcus,

We saw an elevated number of orchestrator reconciliation retries for MediSync's private deployment starting ~09:20 PST. Symptoms: a series of leader re-elections in the node pool, increased control-channel latency (~200-600ms p50 for management RPCs), and subsequent transient agent reconnects. The rolling upgrade that began at 08:45 likely coincided with an expensive reconciliation job that queued on the control-plane leader and caused the reconciliation loop to pile up.

I attached an initial log bundle (reconciliation-logs-20261127.tar.gz) with reconciler traces and leader election timestamps.

Immediate actions taken:
- Throttled the reconciliation job on the leader at 09:34 (temporary mitigation)
- Bumped orchestration timeouts for agent heartbeats to reduce flaps
- Flagged the remainder of the rolling upgrade to pause until we validate the config change

Next steps I recommend: confirm whether MediSync ran any config recalculations on their side during the window and schedule a short bridge with their ops to review the leader history.

-Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Technical Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Orchestrator reconciliation backlog detected on your VPC (MediSync)

Hannah — quick technical notes following the bridge:

Root-cause hypothesis: during the 08:45 rolling upgrade a synchronous reconciliation task (full-state diffs for a config change) ran on the elected leader concurrently with leader-to-follower snapshot streaming. The reconciliation task holds a reconciliation lock and spawns many cache refreshes; with the leader processing these heavy diffs, follower throughput dropped and multiple short re-elections happened as pick-leader timed out under load.

Why this mattered: the reconciliation concurrency and leader CPU exhaustion drove control-plane RPC latency up, which in turn caused agent reconnect backoffs. Once the leader throttled reconciliation at 09:34, election stability returned.

Mitigation and short-term recommendations (we did the first two):
- Make reconciliation tasks opportunistic (non-blocking) during upgrades — we have a config flag to enable this
- Pause heavyweight reconciliation jobs while a rolling upgrade is active (recommended)
- Increase leader election timeout during known maintenance windows
- Post-upgrade, run a controlled quiesce sweep to let caches repopulate before resuming heavy jobs

I attached a small runbook we can share with MediSync ops that lists the exact commands and the telemetry to monitor (runbook-orch-reconcile-steps.csv).

I'll prepare a timeline for the postmortem doc and proposed code/config changes; Hannah, want me to draft the technical note for your customer-facing summary?

- Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — MediSync private VPC (rolling upgrade 2026-11-27)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for joining the bridge. Below is a concise post-incident summary and our proposed action items. Please let me know if you'd like this expanded into a formal postmortem slide deck.

Timeline (brief):
- 08:45 PST: Redwood orchestrator rolling upgrade starts
- ~09:20 PST: Elevated reconciliation queue and leader CPU spikes observed
- 09:34 PST: Redwood applies reconciliation throttle and pauses further heavy jobs
- 09:40–09:55 PST: Short agent reconnects observed; no data-plane request failures recorded
- 10:15 PST: Upgrade paused to validate config changes

Impact: brief control-plane latency spikes and short-lived reconnects; no customer-facing inference errors recorded.

Root cause: a synchronous full-state reconciliation task ran on the control-plane leader during the rolling upgrade, saturating leader CPU and triggering leader-election timeouts.

Actions we have taken (completed):
- Paused rolling upgrade and resumed after validation window
- Applied a reconciliation concurrency throttle (temporary)
- Increased leader election timeout for MediSync's cluster during maintenance windows
- Collected and shared logs: reconciliation-logs-20261127.tar.gz

Proposed follow-ups (proposal):
1) Schedule a maintenance window to apply an orchestrator patch that makes reconciliations opportunistic (non-blocking) — ETA: next week (proposal: 2026-12-07 09:00–09:45 PST).
2) Run a controlled cache rehydrate sweep after future upgrades (we can automate this in your upgrade playbook).
3) Add a short pre-upgrade check to detect any pending heavy reconciliation tasks and postpone upgrades if needed.

Request for approval: can we run deeper log collection (additional sampling) on your nodes between 2026-12-01 and 2026-12-03 for 2 hours? This will help validate the opportunistic reconciliation behavior in a staging window.

Credits/comp: we're flagging this incident for review with our support policy team; I will confirm any service credit eligibility by 2026-12-04.

Attached: runbook-orch-reconcile-steps.csv (operational steps and monitoring knobs)
Related artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ORCH-9012 (internal Jira), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPostmortemMediSync

Thanks,
Hannah
